title: Canary heartbeats + adaptive backpressure for multi-region failover and SLO preservation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce a lightweight, minimally-invasive canary heartbeat tier and an SLO-driven adaptive backpressure system to stabilize autoscaling and prevent cascading capacity loss during regional overloads. The goal is to preserve customer-facing P95 latency and error-rate SLOs by making health signals more actionable and reducing oscillation in the autoscaler when cross-region failovers or traffic spikes occur.
motivation: Recent incidents showed that coarse readiness aggregation and undifferentiated liveness failures caused aggressive scaling churn and cross-region failover cascades. We need finer-grained signals that separate critical request-serving readiness from soft degradations, plus an automated backpressure policy that sheds low-priority traffic before scale storms hit the fleet.
acceptance_criteria: Add a 'canary-heartbeat' health class that runs synthetic lightweight requests exercising routing, KV cache warmup, and model variant fallback without consuming full GPU transient resources
Implement an SLO-indexed priority for traffic buckets (control plane, paid customers, free tier, internal telemetry) and expose this to the backpressure decision path
Autoscaler damping improved: reduce scale up/down oscillations by 40% in synthetic spike tests compared to baseline
During a simulated regional outage, system preserves P95 latency for high-priority customers in other regions while shedding low-priority traffic gracefully
Health signal composition documented and surfaced in Console: canary-heartbeat, fast-readiness, slow-readiness, binary-liveness
E2E test harness that can inject synthetic canary failures and measure rollback/failover time under controlled overloads
implementation_notes: Canary heartbeats will be a separate readiness class; they run at a low QPS and use short-sequence prompts to exercise model routing and cache warm paths
Do not route canary heartbeats through GPU cold-start intensive paths; use a lightweight CPU-validated path that still touches the routing code
Backpressure controller will consume SLO profile per-customer from Console config and compute an eviction score combining priority, recent error budget burn, and regional capacity delta
Expose a feature flag to enable gradual rollout of canary heartbeats in staging then canary regions
Autoscaler hysteresis: implement a two-tier damping window (short window for soft increases, longer window for declines) and tie thresholds to canary success rate
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Canary heartbeats could create false positives if synthetic prompts don't reflect production patterns. Mitigation: use a mix of short/medium synthetic prompts derived from top-k production templates and rotate them weekly

Risk: Priority-based shedding may upset customers with bursts. Mitigation: provide transparent Console dashboards and allow per-customer guardrails with throttling instead of hard drops for premium customers
Risk: Complexity in autoscaler logic increases maintenance burden. Mitigation: keep decision path deterministic, log every backpressure decision and provide a replay tool for offline analysis
tasks: API: add health-class field to probe registration and propagate to runtime (ENG-87244-API)
Runtime: implement lightweight canary handler and synthetic prompt templates (ENG-87244-RUNTIME)
Controller: backpressure decision engine and priority eviction queue (ENG-87244-CONTROLLER)
Console: dashboard for canary heartbeats, eviction events, and per-customer SLO burn rate (ENG-87244-CONSOLE)
Testing: build chaos tests for multi-region failover and ramp tests for autoscaler hysteresis (ENG-87244-TESTS)
Docs: runbook and postmortem template updates for health-signal driven incidents
progress_updates: 2026-01-22: Spike completed for synthetic prompt set generation. We captured top-20 templates across chat/generation and distilled 3 low-cost canary templates.
2026-01-30: Runtime prototype added a new health-class flag and a CPU path for canary requests. Benchmarks show <5% additional CPU per host at 1QPS canary rate.
2026-02-05: Backpressure decision algorithm v0 merged behind feature flag; uses priority + regional capacity delta. Initial local tests look promising but need chaos validation.
2026-02-12: Integration test harness added to CI with two-region topology; observed reduced autoscaler oscillation during synthetic spike when canary success rate used as gating signal.
2026-02-15: Rolling enablement plan drafted for staging and canary regions; Console panels for canary health wired to metrics but pending visual polish
notes: Coordinator: pair with SRE on incident runbooks and define SLO burn thresholds that flip backpressure from advisory to enforced
Plan to run a customer-facing communication for premium customers before any hard-shedding experiments
